children: Andre Loranger has been appointed as Britain's next National Statistician, the U.K. Statistics Authority said Tuesday, overseeing the publication of national data that has faced concerns in recent years over its reliability.
Loranger, currently Chief Statistician of Canada, takes over from Emma Rourke, who stepped down in December 2025. She replaced Ian Diamond, who resigned in May 2025 due to health issues.

Diamond's departure came shortly before the publication of a government review of the Office for National Statistics that criticized its management. The role of the U.K.'s top statistician was split last year, with a civil servant now serving as its permanent secretary.

The National Statistician role is the top adviser to the country's statistics authority and government on the quality of official statistics. The ONS has faced challenges from lawmakers over its reliability, suspended its top labor-market survey, and temporarily delayed retail sales and producer-price data over quality issues.

The Bank of England, which uses ONS figures as a basis for its decisions on monetary policy, repeatedly raised concerns about the ONS amid a deterioration of jobs-market data. In common with some other data agencies globally, the ONS has faced falling response rates and squeezed budgets.

Loranger, who has been at Canada's statistics agency for 29 years, will take up his five-year term this fall, the U.K. Statistics Authority said. His recruitment from Canada echoes the hiring of the-then central-bank governor Mark Carney to lead the BOE in 2013. Carney is now Canada's prime minister.

"[Loranger's] deep experience in Canada and on the international stage will accelerate our work to unlock greater value across the U.K. statistical system for users, by increasing engagement and supporting a culture of openness and innovation," said Penny Young, interim chair of the U.K. Statistics Authority.
Statistics Canada is now deciding on interim leadership for when Loranger leaves in mid-October, spokesman Carter Mann said.
"A separate process to appoint a new chief statistician is also underway, and an announcement will be made by the government of Canada once the appointment has been finalized," he added.
